1.

Heard Sri Shreesh Kumar Mishra Atal, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Rajesh Kumar Singh,
learned A.G.A.-I for the State and perused the entire record.
2.  However, no one appeared on behalf of respondent Nos.2 to 4 to argue the instant jail appeal despite names of Sri Amit Kumar Awasthi and Sri Ashish Mishra have been shown in the cause list.

3. Under challenge in this criminal appeal/jail appeal under Section 383 read with Section 374(2)
Cr.P.C. is the impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022 passed by learned Additional District and Sessions Judge/ Special Judge, POCSO Act, Court No.2, District Lucknow in Sessions Trial No.1179/2017 : State of U.P. vs. Raj Prakash Soni arising out of Case Crime No.792/2017, under Section 377 of Indian Penal Code, 18601 and Sections 3/4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 20122, Police Station Gazipur, District Lucknow, whereby the appellant has been convicted and sentenced to undergo seven years rigorous imprisonment for the offence under Section 4 of POCSO Act with a fine of Rs.5,000/- and in default of payment of fine, he has further been directed to undergo six months' additional imprisonment.
4.

sentences.text: The prosecution's case, in brief is that on 24.09.2017 when the victim, who is son of first informant, Mukesh Kumar Yadav (P.W.1) aged about 4 years was playing at his house.
The neighbour accused/appellant came to his house and lured his son, the victim.
Thereafter he took the son of the informant in his room and had inserted his male genital part in his anus.
When the victim came to his house, he was crying and blood was oozing from his anus.
The first informant asked the victim as to why is victim crying, his son told that Pranjal's father, the appellant had inserted his male genital part in his anus.

5. On the basis of aforesaid, written report, Ext. Ka-1 submitted by the first informant, Mukesh Kumar Yadav, the first information report, Ext. Ka-2 came to be lodged against the accused/
appellant under Section 377 I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act.

6. After registration of the case, the Investigating Officer recorded the statements of the witnesses under Section 161 of Code of Criminal Procedure3, prepared the site plan, Ext. Aa-2 and upon completion of investigation, submitted charge-sheet, Ext. Aa-3 against accused-appellant for the offence under Section 377 I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act.
7. Charges for the offences under Section 377 I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act was framed against the accused/ appellant, who denied the charges and claimed to be tried.

8. In order to bring home guilt of the accused/ appellant, the prosecution has examined Mukesh Kumar Yadav, complainant as P.W.-1, Victim as P.W.-2, Lady Constable, Saroj Devi as P.W.-3, Dr.
Mohd. Kasim as P.W.-4.
9.
The accused/ appellant, in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C., has stated the prosecution story to be false.
He has also stated to have been falsely implicated in this case.
He also claimed to be innocent.

2 10.
No evidence in defence was adduced by the accused/ appellant before the learned trial court.

11. The learned trial court, after appreciating the evidence available on record, rendered the impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022 whereby the accused/ appellant came to be convicted as aforesaid.

12. Aggrieved by the aforesaid impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022, the accused/
appellant has preferred the instant jail appeal.

13. Submission of learned counsel for the appellant is that the finding of guilt of the accused/
appellant arrived at by the learned trial court is perverse and contrary to the evidence available on record.
14. His further submission is that the appellant is innocent, who has been falsely implicated in this case because of enmity with father of the victim.

He has further submitted that there are material contradictions in the testimonies of prosecution witnesses i.e. P.W.1- Mukesh Kumar Yadav, the first informant and P.W.2, who is victim of the case, which were not appreciated by the learned trial court in the correct perspective while giving the finding of guilt against the appellant.
Therefore, the conviction of the appellant under Section 4 of POCSO Act and the sentences awarded therefor are palpably illegal and deserve to be set aside.

15. His further submission is that the appellant has already served out sentence awarded by the learned trial court by means of impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022 which is also evident from custody certificate issued by District Jail Lucknow which reveals that the appellant has been released on 17.05.2024 on completion of sentence and deposit of fine which was awarded to him by means of impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022.
He has further submitted that the sentence awarded to the appellant is highly excessive which deserves to be modified in the facts of this case.
16. Learned for the accused/ appellant has, thus, prayed to set aside the impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022 and to acquit the accused/ appellant accordingly.

17. Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has submitted that the accused/ appellant rightly came to be convicted vide impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022, which is well discussed and reasoned.
The accused/ appellant was named in the first information report.
The prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of cogent and reliable testimonies of prosecution witnesses.
18. He has further submitted that the learned trial court, after due appreciation of the testimonies of prosecution witnesses, has rightly given the finding of conviction of the appellant.

Therefore,
interference by this Court is neither warranted nor justified.
He, accordingly, prays for dismissal of the instant jail appeal.

3 19.
Learned A.G.A. has further submitted that the victim is aged about 4 years only.
There is no evidence on record to show that the appellant has been falsely implicated in this case for some other reason or due to enmity between the appellant and the father of the victim.

He has further submitted that in light of clear and cogent testimonies of P.W.1, the first informant and P.W.2, the victim as also having regard to the presumption which is available by virtue of Section 42 of POCSO Act, the finding of guilt of appellant has rightly been recorded by learned trial court and having regard to the tender age of the victim, the appellant has rightly been convicted for a period of seven years rigorous imprisonment which cannot be said to be excessive and disproportionate of the offence which he has committed.
He has further submitted that the present appeal is devoid of merit which deserve to be dismissed.

20. Section 42 of POCSO Act being germane to the controversy is quoted herein below :
"42 Alternate punishment - Where an act or omission constitutes an offence punishable under this Act and also under sections 166A, 354A, 354B, 354C, 354D,
370, 370A, 375, 376, 376A, 376AB, 376B, 376C, 376D, 376DA, 376DB, 376E, section 509 of the Indian Penal Code or section 67B of the Information Technology Act,
2000 (21 of 2000), then, notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, the offender found guilty of such offence shall be liable to punishment only under this Act or under the Indian Penal Code as provides for punishment which is greater in degree."

21. Having heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned A.G.A. for the State and upon perusal of the record, it transpires that the first information report came to be lodged against the present appellant by P.W.1- Mukesh Kumar Yadav, who is father of the victim.
The P.W.1 is proved the written report as Ext. Ka-1 by stating that on 24.09.2017, his four years old son, the victim told him that the appellant had inserted his male genital part in his anus.
When the first informant inspected the anus of the victim, he shows that the same is bleeding.
P.W.2, who is victim is aged about four years only.
He has also stated that the accused-appellant is father of child named Pranjal.
According to this witness, he was taken into a corner of kitchen after disrobing the victim and himself he inserted male genital part into anus of the victim which caused the victim immense pain.
He has stated that the victim informed his father about entire incident.

The medical report of the victim has been proved by Dr. Mohd. Kasim (P.W.4) as exhibit Ka-3, this Court finds that the statement of victim (P.W.2) is very clear and cogent on the issue that on the date of incident the appellant inserted his male genital part into his anus, therefore, committing offences as defined under Section 377 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.

The statement of victim (P.W.2)
corroborates the prosecution story as contained in Ka-1 which was submitted by father of the victim (P.W.1).
The testimony of the aforesaid witnesses of fact, namely, P.W.1, the first informant and P.W.2, the victim are clear and cogent on the issue.
When read in light of the medical evidence, the same establishes guilt of accused-appellant for offence under Section 377 and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act beyond any reasonable doubt.

22. Having considered the entire prosecution evidence available on record, this Court does not find any plausible reason for false implication of the appellant in this case as argued by learned counsel.

Thus, this court does not find any illegality or irregularly in the impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022 whereby the appellant was held guilty for offence under Section 4 of POCSO Act and has been sentenced to seven years rigorous imprisonment.
The present appeal deserves to be dismissed and is, accordingly, dismissed.

23. As learned A.G.A. has informed that the appellant has already been released on 17.05.2024 from jail where he was lodged after serving out entire sentence awarded to him for offence under Section 4 of POCSO Act and he has also deposited fine which was imposed by the learned trial court by means of impugned judgment and order dated 03.12.2022, therefore, he need not surrender.
24. Let the trial court record along with a copy of this judgment be transmitted forthwith to the learned trial Court concerned for information and necessary compliance through fax/ e-mail.
(Ajai Kumar Srivastava-I, J.) Order Date :- 11.12.2024
